summary: A 1917 Weather Bureau lookout erected at this Lincoln National Forest site in 1937; NRHP-listed 1988; the tower itself is not open to the public.

access.note: Reached on foot. The Forest Service page, last updated February 19, 2025, says the tower itself is not available to the public and carries a 'Site Closed' label.

corrections.why: The Forest Service and the register's description both say the tower was built in 1917 for the Weather Bureau and erected on this site in 1937. The record's 1937 is the erection date that the register's Built field gives.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1917 is the build date for the original Weather Bureau structure; 1937 is when it was sold to the Forest Service and erected at this site. The register's Built field lists only 1937.

notes_for_editor: Access: the record says public, citing a recreation.gov listing. The Forest Service page (updated February 19, 2025) says the tower itself is not available to the public and carries a Site Closed label, so facts.access is set to restricted. Please check recreation.gov before publishing. The cab maker is disputed across sources (Aermotor LX-24 versus International Derrick), but the record's design string states LX-24 as fact. The March 16, 1933 item is known only through the Forest Lookouts transcription and was not checked against the newspaper; it conflicts with a 1937 erection on this site unless an earlier lookout stood here. Current staffing is unknown. No fire or abandonment was found. Cabin rental was proposed in the 2020 report; no later rental listing was found. height_m 13.7 is the register's 45 ft. The record's 2015 NHLR registration and 1988 NRHP date match the sources.
